sentences.text: Arthurdactylus was a medium-sized pterosaur with a wingspan of 4.5 to 4.6 meters and a body mass of 15 kilograms.
It possessed relatively long wings and exceptionally long wing fingers compared to its 22-centimeter torso, possibly more so than any other pterodactyloid.
The hind limbs of Arthurdactylus were weakly developed.
The genus was named in 1994 by Eberhard Frey and David Martill to honor Arthur Conan Doyle, the author of The Lost World.
The holotype specimen, cataloged as SMNK 1133 PAL, is a reasonably complete skeleton missing the skull, neck, sternum, and some tail vertebrae.
The authors initially spelled the species name with a hyphenated diacritic that was later corrected to conandoylei in 1998.
The original describers classified Arthurdactylus within the family Ornithocheiridae.
Arthurdactylus lived during the Early Cretaceous in the Crato Formation of northeastern Brazil.
It lived between 119.57 and 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
Paleontologist Alexander Kellner suggests that Arthurdactylus is more closely related to the Anhangueridae, differing from the original classification.
